core_obligations: Define the functor and check continuity (proof lines 3038-3046): by the definition of etaleness of a morphism of algebraic spaces the rule sending an object U -> X to the composite U -> Y actually defines a functor j, which is cocontinuous and continuous simply because coverings of the composite object are the same thing as coverings of the original object.

Compare with the localization functor (proof lines 3048-3062): extend j to the categories of objects etale over the spaces and consider the commutative inner square of the resulting diagram; the extended functor is identified with the localization functor at X, so by the localization lemma it induces the same morphism of topoi as the projection v from the localized category.

Conclude (proof lines 3062-3068): by the composition lemma the commutativity of the inner square of cocontinuous functors gives a commutative diagram of the associated morphisms of topoi, which combined with the construction of the small morphism identifies the morphism induced by j with f_{small}, and the explicit formula for the pullback follows from the criterion for a continuous and cocontinuous functor.
proof_roadmap: Check that the rule on objects is a continuous and cocontinuous functor.
Identify its extension to the big sites with a localization functor and invoke the localization lemma.
Use the composition lemma and the construction of the small morphism to identify the morphisms of topoi, and read off the pullback formula.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for an etale morphism of algebraic spaces the rule sending an object etale over the source to its composite with the morphism is a continuous and cocontinuous functor on the small etale sites which induces the morphism of topoi f_{small}, so that the pullback of a sheaf is computed by evaluating on the image object (statement lines 3021-3036). The proof (proof lines 3038-3071) checks continuity and cocontinuity, identifies the extension of the functor to the big sites with a localization functor, and compares the induced morphisms of topoi through the localization and composition lemmas. H2: a comparison of morphisms of topoi with three inputs, written out in full.
